4) Any certificate management constraints (for mTLS) and whether your team can upload client certs or prefers API-key-based auth initially.

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Following up with the technical details Lauren promised. Below are the typical options we support and practical guidance for each. Happy to review this in the deep dive next week.

1) Preferred: VPC Endpoint / PrivateLink (AWS) or Private Service Connect (GCP)
- No public egress required from your app instances; traffic stays on the cloud provider network.
- We expose an endpoint service; your infra team creates an interface endpoint in the customer VPC and optionally sets up private DNS so the Redwood API hostname resolves to the endpoint IPs.
- Firewall/security group: allow outbound TCP 443 to the interface endpoint IPs; inbound rules are handled by the provider.
- Benefits: shortest path, avoids public IP allowlisting, simpler to audit.

2) Backup: Public egress + IP allowlist
- If PrivateLink isn't an option, you can egress to public Redwood endpoints but we can provide a set of stable egress IPs (published in the onboarding doc) for you to allow in your firewall.
- Note: If you use a shared NAT egress, we'll need the NAT public IPs (or the range) that your requests will originate from.

3) DNS and TLS considerations
- For PrivateLink, we recommend enabling private DNS so the Redwood hostname resolves inside your VPC to the endpoint IPs. If you cannot modify DNS, we can provide endpoint IPs but you'll need to manage the mapping.
- All traffic is TLS (443). We support TLS1.2+ and strongly recommend TLS1.3 where available.

4) mTLS (mutual TLS)
- We do support mutual TLS for customers that require client cert authentication. Two deployment patterns:
  a) mTLS over PrivateLink: your app presents a client cert to our edge when establishing the TLS connection. We validate client cert CN/SAN and/or an attached client identity token.
  b) mTLS with public endpoints (less common): works the same but requires NAT/public IP routing.
- For mTLS we can accept either:
  - Customer-managed client certs (you provide public cert thumbprints or certs) OR
  - Redwood-issued short-lived client certs (we can automate issuance if you have an internal CA integration).

5) Auth patterns (SDK)
- Short term (fastest): API keys scoped to project + route-based RBAC. Keys delivered over a secure vault (not checked into code).
- Long term (recommended for private deployments): mTLS + per-route tokens or signed requests for stronger assurance.

Sample security group / firewall rule (example)
- Outbound: Allow TCP 443 to destination (Redwood endpoint IPs or interface endpoint IDs).
- If using IP allowlist: Allow outbound from app subnet to Redwood egress IPs (we'll provide the list as part of onboarding).

What we need from you to prepare:
- Network diagram (VPC layout), CIDRs (app subnets, NAT public IPs if applicable).
- Any egress proxy/firewall that performs SSL inspection. If present, include the product and whether it supports passing client certs through.
- Whether your security team requires mTLS or if API-key is sufficient initially.

I'll prepare a short design doc based on what you share and bring a checklist to the deep dive.

—Jonas

Thanks Lauren / Jonas — good write-up. A few answers from our side and a couple of follow-ups: 

Answers:
- CIDR: our primary app VPC is 10.20.0.0/16. App subnets are 10.20.1.0/24 and 10.20.2.0/24.
- Egress: we egress through a shared NAT gateway with static public IPs (we'll provide exact NAT IPs).
- TLS interception: we do not perform TLS interception on outbound.
- mTLS: security would prefer mTLS, but we can start with API-key scoped access for the POC and then move to mTLS for prod.

Questions:
1) If we go PrivateLink, can we still enable mTLS?
2) If we start with API keys for the POC, what are the recommended rotation practices?
3) Timeline: Can we do the technical deep dive on Wed 8/5 at 10:00 AM PT? Olivia (CC'd) is our infra lead and will join.

Appreciate the checklist attachment — we'll share the network diagram + NAT IPs by EOD tomorrow.
